answer:
The computational domain is parameterised by three user-supplied values: Lx (domain length in x), Ly (domain height in y), and Lcol (width of the initial water column, with Lcol < Lx).
The mesh is 2D: one cell in the z-direction, with the frontAndBack boundary patch set to type empty.
The in-plane mesh is a rectangular block of nx by ny cells spanning [0, Lx] in x and [0, Ly] in y, with nx and ny also parameterised.
The water column occupies the region 0 <= x < Lcol and 0 <= y < Ly; everywhere else is air.
A setFields utility is run at startup to set alpha.water = 1 inside the column region and alpha.water = 0 outside it.
In system/controlDict, the application is interFoam.
Time stepping uses adjustableRunTime with a user-supplied deltaT and a maxCo of 1.
The initial velocity field U is set to (0 0 0) everywhere.
The initial pressure field p is set to the hydrostatic distribution: p = (1 - alpha.water) * (rho_l - rho_g) * g * (Ly - y).
All four wall patches (leftWall, rightWall, bottomWall, topWall) use noSlip for U, fixedFluxPressure for p, and zeroGradient for alpha.water. This closed-box configuration is a deliberate choice to observe the full sloshing dynamics without outflow; it is documented as a comment in each boundary file.
The topWall is treated as a solid no-slip wall consistent with the closed-box choice, not as an open-atmosphere boundary.
Physical constants use standard water-air values: rho_l = 998.2 kg/m^3, rho_g = 1.225 kg/m^3, nu_l = 1e-5 m^2/s, nu_g = 1.5e-5 m^2/s, sigma = 0.072 N/m.
Gravity is set to (0 -9.81 0) in constant/g.
The pRefCell is set to the cell index at the top-centre of the domain and pRef to 0 Pa.
No outflow, inlet, or pressure-vent boundary condition is applied anywhere.
